A card that turns selected (its outline goes from line to state)
The current navigation item (a bar on its start edge)

join.markup: (data-join="block" for stacked parts)

forcedColors.what: Windows contrast themes (and other forced-colour modes) replace every colour with a few system colours, remove box-shadows and background images, and keep borders and outlines (drawn in the system text colour — transparent ones too).
tokensCss: ARIA states (aria-selected, aria-current, aria-pressed, aria-checked) and labels around a checked radio (segmented controls, choice cards) get an inside outline in SelectedItem, as wide as a state border
disabled controls and their borders turn GrayText
you: give every control a border, transparent if the design shows none (BR-06)
never draw a ring or a boundary with box-shadow alone (BR-05, BR-06)
show selection with an attribute tokens.css knows (aria-selected, aria-current, aria-pressed, aria-checked), a label around a checked radio, or a real border — not a fill alone
don't set forced-color-adjust: none except on colour swatches and charts, where the colours are the content

classes.use: Parts that touch (a button group, a segmented control, an input with its button): borders overlap by one control width so each seam is one line; outer corners keep their radius; the hovered, selected and focused part is lifted
The same, stacked: list items or accordion panels that touch

checks.title: Focus ring ≥ 2px thick with an offset (colour checked in C3)
Widths are whole pixels from 1 to 3px on the scale — no hairlines below a pixel — and px in code, so a line stays a line at 200% text
Jobs stay apart: a state is wider than the control it marks, jobs that share a width use different colours, and the focus ring stands off the element
Lines people need — control boundaries, states, the current-item bar — reach 3:1 against every background, in Light and Dark
States don't move content: a wider border takes its extra width off the padding, and at least 2px of padding is left in every density
Joined parts share one line: parts overlap by the control width and the part that changes is lifted above its neighbours
Forced colours (Windows contrast themes) keep every cue: the focus ring is an outline, states get a system-colour outline, disabled controls turn GrayText, overlays keep a border

rules.rule: Border widths come from a job: border-width is var(--ds-border-width-line), -control, -state or -indicator (Tailwind border-line, border-control, border-state, border-indicator and their side forms: border-b-line, border-s-indicator, divide-y-line). No px, rem or em numbers; 0 only to remove a side.
rules.why: A hard-coded width doesn't follow the product's control width, and a 2px border in the wrong place reads as a selected state.

rules.rule: Never use border width primitives (--ds-border-width-1, -2, -3) in components. Pick the job.
rules.why: Primitives don't say what a line is for, and don't move when the product changes its control width.

rules.rule: No hairlines and no text-relative widths: nothing below 1px (0.5px, thin, a 1px line scaled down with transform), and never rem or em widths.
rules.why: Below a pixel a line looks different in every browser (Chrome and Edge round it up to 1px; Safari and Firefox can draw a single device pixel on high-density screens); rem widths double at 200% text, so every 1px line becomes 2px — the width of a state.

rules.rule: In Tailwind use the ds widths (border-line … border-indicator), not border, border-2, border-[3px] or ring-* for boundaries.
rules.why: Tailwind's numbers are a second set of widths no check covers, and ring-* draws with box-shadow, which forced colours remove.

rules.rule: Never remove the focus ring: no outline: none or outline: 0 (Tailwind outline-none) on :focus or :focus-visible unless an outline replaces it. A box-shadow ring keeps a transparent outline beside it.
rules.why: Keyboard users lose their place; a box-shadow ring is removed in forced colours, so the element has no ring there at all.

rules.rule: Boundaries that carry meaning are borders or outlines, never box-shadow or a background alone: a control without a visible border gets border: var(--ds-border-width-control) solid transparent.
rules.why: Forced colours (Windows contrast themes) replace every fill with one system colour and remove shadows: a button or field shown only by its fill or a box-shadow disappears. A transparent border is drawn there in the system's text colour.

rules.rule: The colour fits the job: control, state and indicator widths take a colour that reaches 3:1 (color.border.input, color.border.strong, color.action.secondary.border, color.border.selected, color.border.danger / warning / success). color.border.subtle and color.border.default are for lines that only separate or outline.
rules.why: A decorative grey on a field's edge measures under 3:1: people with low vision can't find the field.

rules.rule: A state never shows by border colour alone: a selected, invalid or current border also widens to its job (state, indicator) and comes with a check mark, an icon or a message.
rules.why: A red 1px border next to a grey one differs mostly in hue; for many people with red-green colour blindness the two look alike.

rules.rule: A state that widens a border takes the extra width off the padding, written on the tokens: calc(var(--ds-space-inset-md) - (var(--ds-border-width-state) - var(--ds-border-width-control))). The content must not move.
rules.why: A wider border pushes the label sideways on every selection; in a list, every row's text jumps as the selection moves.

rules.rule: Parts that touch use .ds-join (it overlaps their borders by one control width and lifts the part that changes); never two borders side by side, and never a hand-made negative margin.
rules.why: Two 1px borders make a 2px seam — the width of a selected state — between parts that are meant to read as one.

rules.rule: Never redefine border or focus variables in app code (--ds-border-width-*, --ds-focus-ring-*). Change border.control or border.roles in the engine config and build.
rules.why: An overridden width skips the checks that keep jobs apart, colours at 3:1 and states from moving content.

decisions.what: Does it need a line at all
decisions.question: What should the boundary do?
answers: Group things that belong together, with room to spare
space (Spacing: a bigger stack or inline gap) — no line
Set a region apart from the page (a sidebar, a header band, a well)

a surface change (color.bg.surface-sunken, an elevation level) — no line; in forced colours both surfaces become the page colour, so a region that holds controls or must be found keeps a border.width.line edge
Separate items that sit close together (list rows, table rows, menu groups)
border.width.line with color.border.subtle
Outline a card, a panel, a table frame or a menu
border.width.line with color.border.default (things that float: their level's edge, elevation.floating.border)
Show where a control is (a field, a checkbox, a secondary button)
border.width.control with color.border.input (fields, checkboxes, radios) or color.action.secondary.border (buttons)

decisions.question: What changed?
answers: It is selected (an option, a card, a segment)
border.width.state with color.border.selected, plus a check mark or bold label
It is in error, needs attention or passed
border.width.state with color.border.danger / warning / success, plus an icon and a message
It is the current one (the tab, the page in the navigation, a row being edited)
border.width.indicator on one side (block-end for tabs, inline-start for navigation) with color.border.selected, and aria-current or aria-selected
It has keyboard focus
nothing to set: tokens.css draws the focus ring on :focus-visible
It is hovered or pressed
a fill (color.bg.state-hover, color.bg.item-hover) — not a border; the width stays the same
It is disabled
color.action.disabled.border at the same width; tokens.css turns it GrayText in forced colours

decisions.what: A state that widens the border
decisions.question: How do you keep the content still?
answers: A control that turns selected or invalid
padding-inline: calc(var(--ds-space-inset-md) - (var(--ds-border-width-state) - var(--ds-border-width-control)))
A card that turns selected
padding: calc(var(--ds-space-inset-lg) - (var(--ds-border-width-state) - var(--ds-border-width-line)))
The current navigation item
padding-inline-start: calc(var(--ds-space-inset-md) - var(--ds-border-width-indicator))
A tab
nothing: its bar is a ::after on the selected tab only (position: absolute along the block-end edge), so nothing moves

decisions.question: Do they read as one thing?
answers: Yes: a button group, a segmented control, an input with its button, stacked list items
.ds-join (or data-join="block"): parts overlap by one control border, so each seam is one line
No: separate things side by side
a gap (Spacing), each with its own border
Table cells
border-collapse: collapse, or lines on one side only (border-block-end on rows)

decisions.question: How is the ring drawn?
answers: On anything focusable
tokens.css draws it: an outline, focus.ring.width wide, focus.ring.offset away, focus.ring.color
You need a different look (an inset ring on a full-width row)
keep the outline and change outline-offset (a negative offset draws it inside) — never box-shadow alone
Removing the default ring
never without a replacement outline; box-shadow rings vanish in forced colours

mistakes.measured: Chromium (Chrome, Edge) rounds it up and draws a full 1px on every screen (measured: computed 1px at 1× and 2×); Safari and Firefox can draw a single device pixel on high-density screens — one token, two looks, and never thinner than 1px on a 1× screen
mistakes.fixValue: 1px everywhere; quieter by colour (1.58:1 on bg/surface), not by width

mistakes.mistake: A card-outline grey on a text field (color.border.default)
mistakes.measured: 1.84:1 against bg/surface — under the 3:1 a field's edge needs

mistakes.mistake: An error shown only by turning the field's border red
mistakes.measured: the red and the normal grey have the same lightness (1.00:1 between them); with protanopia their difference drops from 0.166 to 0.088 (OKLab) — the two borders look nearly the same
mistakes.fixValue: 2px against 1px, so the change shows without colour; with an icon and a message

mistakes.mistake: Widening a selected control's border from 1px to 2px without touching its padding
mistakes.measured: the label moves 1px sideways each time it is selected
mistakes.fixValue: 11px of padding instead of 12px: the border grows inward, the label stays still

mistakes.mistake: Two bordered buttons placed side by side
mistakes.measured: their two 1px borders make a 2px seam — the width of a selected state
mistakes.fixValue: parts overlap by 1px: every seam is one 1px line

mistakes.mistake: A focus ring drawn with box-shadow and outline: none
mistakes.measured: forced colours remove every box-shadow: the element has no ring at all there
mistakes.fixValue: 2px outline, 2px away; in forced colours it takes the system's Highlight

mistakes.mistake: A primary button with border: none (its fill is its only edge)
mistakes.measured: forced colours replace its fill with the page colour: only the label is left, with nothing to show it is a button
mistakes.fixValue: invisible in normal colours; drawn in the system text colour in forced colours

mistakes.measured: at 200% text it becomes 2px — the width of a selected state — on every line in the product
